name: Decision-making in changing or interactive environments
gist: Theory for learning strategies in settings where the problem changes over time, the learner gets feedback through actions, or multiple agents are interacting.
explain: Most learning theory assumes the world is static: the rules do not change between the time you train a model and the time you use it. But in reality, the world shifts. A spam filter trained on 2023 spam must handle spam tactics from 2025. A recommendation system trained on one year of user preferences must adapt as trends evolve. A robot trained to grasp one type of object must adapt when objects change shape or texture. This subtheme asks: how can a learner make good decisions when the environment itself is learning or changing?

The difficulty is that you cannot simply retrain on old data; the old data no longer reflects reality. Additionally, in interactive settings, your own actions change what happens next — if a robot reaches for a fragile object, it learns to be gentler, but this changes the feedback it receives. In game-theoretic scenarios, you have multiple agents learning simultaneously, each trying to predict what the others will do, leading to circular reasoning. The learner must balance exploiting what it has learned (choosing actions it thinks are good) with exploring new actions (to learn whether they are even better), because committing entirely to exploration wastes opportunities to use known good actions, while committing entirely to exploitation misses chances to find better actions. Pick the wrong balance and it either gets stuck repeating bad decisions or wastes time on obviously bad ones.

Researchers study these problems using tools from reinforcement learning (learning through trial and error and rewards), online learning (adapting as data arrives one example at a time), and game theory (analyzing multi-agent interactions). They analyze how much the model can drift from its training environment and still perform well, what exploration strategies guarantee finding good solutions in reasonable time, and how to model an opponent's behavior. The work includes studying specific problem structures — bandit problems (pick one option from many), Markov decision processes (environments where the next state depends only on the current state and action), and strategic scenarios where agents anticipate each other's moves.

papers.title: Best-of-three-worlds Analysis for Dueling Bandits with Borda Winner
papers.contribution: Achieves Õ(K^1/3 T^2/3) adversarial regret, O(K log² T / Δ²min) stochastic regret, and O(K log² T / Δ²min + (C² K log² T / Δ²min)^1/3) corrupted regret, matching state-of-the-art individually.

papers.title: Beyond Aggregation: Guiding Clients in Heterogeneous Federated Learning
papers.contribution: Introduces a novel FL paradigm treating heterogeneity as a feature, achieving improvements in model accuracy and client guidance precision compared to standard approaches.

papers.title: Decomposing Extrapolative Problem Solving: Spatial Transfer and Length Scaling with Map Worlds
papers.contribution: Provides principled insights that transfer needs high coverage and modest diversity while scaling critically depends on neighboring-but-longer examples, with RL stabilizing but not exceeding SFT ceilings.

papers.title: Efficient Best-of-Both-Worlds Algorithms for Contextual Combinatorial Semi-Bandits
papers.contribution: The algorithm achieves Õ(√T) regret in adversarial regime and Õ(ln T) regret in stochastic regime with substantial per-round speed-ups.

papers.title: How reinforcement learning after next-token prediction facilitates learning
papers.contribution: They expose optimization mechanisms by which RL improves over next-token prediction, showing RL leverages longer responses to facilitate learning and deriving theoretical bounds for linear models on parity tasks.

papers.title: Incentives in Federated Learning with Heterogeneous Agents
papers.contribution: Achieve logarithmic approximation of cost-minimizing contributions with strategy-proof mechanism using pay-what-you-contribute rule, unique within contribution-based transfers.

papers.title: Memory-Statistics Tradeoff in Continual Learning with Structural Regularization
papers.contribution: Theory shows structural regularization mitigates catastrophic forgetting and achieves comparable performance to joint training.

papers.title: Multi-Armed Bandits with Minimum Aggregated Revenue Constraints
papers.contribution: A lower bound demonstrates that time-horizon dependence is optimal in general and reveals fundamental limitations of free exploration principles.

papers.title: Online Conformal Prediction with Adversarial Feedback via Regret Minimization
papers.contribution: Provides miscoverage guarantees for online conformal prediction under adversarial conditions while achieving reasonable conformal set sizes across stochastic and covariate shift setups.

papers.title: Reshaping Reasoning in LLMs: A Theoretical Analysis of RL Training Dynamics through Pattern Selection
papers.contribution: Explains RL training dynamics showing verifiable rewards enable convergence to optimal strategies when base reasoning is strong, while internal feedback initially improves then potentially degrades performance.

papers.title: Single Index Bandits: Generalized Linear Contextual Bandits with Unknown Reward Functions
papers.contribution: ESTOR achieves nearly optimal regret bound Õ(√T) and extends to high-dimensional sparse settings.

papers.title: A Near-Optimal Best-of-Both-Worlds Algorithm for Federated Bandits
papers.contribution: FedFTRL achieves O(sqrt(T)) regret in adversarial settings, significantly improving over prior state-of-the-art O(T^(2/3)) regret.

papers.title: A Perturbation Approach to Unconstrained Linear Bandits
papers.contribution: Establishes optimal sqrt(P_T) path-length dependencies and proves folklore Omega(sqrt(dT)) lower bound for adversarial linear bandits.

papers.title: Achieving Logarithmic Regret in KL-Regularized Zero-Sum Markov Games
papers.contribution: Logarithmic regret in T with Õ(√T) traditional regret scaling, achieving β^(-1) dependence showing KL regularization provides theoretical sample advantage.

papers.title: Activation Function Design Sustains Plasticity in Continual Learning
papers.contribution: Lightweight, domain-general activation design sustains plasticity in continual learning without extra capacity, validated on class-incremental and non-stationary RL benchmarks.

papers.title: Active Continual Learning with Metaplastic Binary Bayesian Neural Networks
papers.contribution: Sustains learning and strong OOD detection on 1000-task Permuted-MNIST; up to 32× label/update savings on OpenLORIS-Object.

papers.title: Adaptive Personalized Federated Learning via Multi-task Averaging of Kernel Mean Embeddings
papers.contribution: Derives finite-sample guarantees on local excess risks for broad distribution classes and proposes random Fourier features implementation.

papers.title: Adversarially Robust Control of Conditional Value-at-Risk via Rockafellar-Uryasev Conformal Inference
papers.contribution: Asymptotically controls empirical CVaR at target level with finite-sample O(1/√T) conservatism gap, demonstrated on portfolio risk and LLM toxicity mitigation.

papers.title: Asymmetric Synthetic Data Update for Domain Incremental Dataset Distillation
papers.contribution: Effectively mitigates catastrophic forgetting achieving superior performance across continually incoming datasets compared to existing methods.

papers.title: Bandit Social Leaning Dynamics with Exploration Episodes
papers.contribution: The paper demonstrates that exploration failure is typical in episodic social learning, proving that externally driven exploration is necessary even when local exploration occurs organically.

papers.title: Contextual Slate GLM Bandits with Limited Adaptivity
papers.contribution: B-SlateGLinCB achieves O(Nd^{3/2} √T) regret; RS-SlateGLinCB achieves O(Nd√T), both independent of non-linearity parameter κ.

papers.title: Convergence of Two-Timescale Markovian Stochastic Approximations with Applications in Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Establishes first almost sure convergence of temporal difference learning with eligibility traces under off-policy learning with linear function approximation.

papers.title: Correcting Split Selection in Online Decision Trees via Anytime-Valid Inference
papers.contribution: Provides anytime-valid control of false splits under non-stationary settings and improves performance while producing substantially smaller trees than existing Hoeffding Trees.

papers.title: Cross-task Calibration for Asynchronous Federated Continual Learning
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms existing methods in robust and efficient learning in dynamic federated environments with semantic-level task drift handling.

papers.title: DAL: A Practical Prior-Free Black-Box Framework for Piecewise Stationary Bandits
papers.contribution: Consistently surpasses all state-of-the-art methods across diverse non-stationary scenarios including synthetic benchmarks and real-world datasets with theoretical insights.

papers.title: Dependence-Aware Label Aggregation for LLM-as-a-Judge via Ising Models
papers.contribution: We present finite-$K$ examples showing that methods based on conditional independence can flip the Bayes label despite matching per-annotator marginals

papers.title: Diversified Multinomial Logit Contextual Bandits
papers.contribution: Achieve (1-1/(e+1))-approximate regret bound with improved approximation factor over submodular baselines and comparable regret with substantially lower runtime.

papers.title: Efficient Adversarial Attacks on High-dimensional Offline Bandits
papers.contribution: Reveals striking vulnerability of high-dimensional offline bandits to adversarial attacks, establishing this as a key security concern for bandit-based evaluation of generative models.

papers.title: Energy-Structured Low-Rank Adaptation for Continual Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple continual learning benchmarks with improved knowledge compaction.

papers.title: Exact Unlearning in Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Constructs such algorithm for tabular MDPs with regret O(H² √SAT + H³ S² A + H².⁵ S² A/ρ) and establishes lower bound Ω(H√SAT + SAH/ρ), showing near-minimax optimality.

papers.title: Exploration-free Algorithms for Multi-group Mean Estimation
papers.contribution: Tighter regret bounds than existing results; framework extends to contextual settings with provable guarantees.

papers.title: Faster Parameter-Free Regret Matching Algorithms
papers.contribution: Empirically attains O(1/T) convergence rate while maintaining parameter-free status, outperforming standard Regret Matching on Nash equilibrium convergence.

papers.title: Finite and Corruption-Robust Regret Bounds in Online Inverse Linear Optimization under M-Convex Action Sets
papers.contribution: Resolves the open question by proving finite regret bound O(d log d) on M-convex sets and O((C+1)d log d) under adversarial corruption without prior knowledge of corruption magnitude.

papers.title: From Ticks to Flows: Dynamics of Neural Reinforcement Learning in Continuous Environments
papers.contribution: Provides first continuous RL equation describing infinitesimal state distribution changes at each gradient step in the infinite width limit.

papers.title: Frozen Policy Iteration: Computationally Efficient RL under Linear $Q^{\pi}$ Realizability for Deterministic Dynamics
papers.contribution: Achieves optimal regret bound of O(sqrt(d^2H^6T)) for MDPs with stochastic initial states and deterministic transitions without simulator access.

papers.title: GFedCL: Graph-Based Federated Continual Learning with Spatial and Temporal Awareness
papers.contribution: GFedCL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art federated continual learning methods with 27.95% improvement on TinyImageNet while preserving privacy.

papers.title: Improved Dimension Dependence for Bandit Convex Optimization with Gradient Variation
papers.contribution: Results improve bounds for both convex and strongly convex functions, provide gradient-variance and small-loss regret bounds, and establish first gradient-variation bounds for one-point bandit linear optimization and dynamic regret.

papers.title: Instance-Dependent Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning via Maximum Likelihood Estimation
papers.contribution: Establishes instance-dependent regret bound scaling with total reward variance and measurement resolution; regret becomes independent of measurement strategy when observation frequency adapts appropriately.

papers.title: Instance-Dependent Fixed-Budget Pure Exploration in Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: First instance-dependent epsilon-uniform guarantee for fixed-budget exploration, characterizing budget requirements in terms of problem-specific exploration hardness.

papers.title: Laplacian Kernelized Bandit
papers.contribution: Regret bounds scale with effective dimension of multi-user kernel, not user count; outperforms baselines in non-linear settings.

papers.title: Learning in Prophet Inequalities with Noisy Observations
papers.contribution: Establishes that both approaches achieve sharp competitive ratio of 1 - 1/e in i.i.d. setting, and 1/2 ratio for non-identical distributions or with window access to past rewards.

papers.title: Learning to Adapt: In-Context Learning Beyond Stationarity
papers.contribution: GLA achieves lower training and testing errors in non-stationary settings by implementing learnable recency bias, with theoretical findings validated by empirical results.

papers.title: Learning to Answer from Correct Demonstrations
papers.contribution: The novel approach achieves logarithmic sample complexity in reward class cardinality, outperforming likelihood maximization methods in settings with multiple correct demonstrations.

papers.title: Learning to Play Multi-Follower Bayesian Stackelberg Games
papers.contribution: The work provides nearly tight regret bounds showing sublinear dependence on the number of followers under type feedback and discusses lower bounds for the action feedback case.

papers.title: Learning-Augmented Moment Estimation on Time-Decay Models
papers.contribution: The framework provides practical learning-augmented algorithms for fundamental streaming problems with empirical validation on real and synthetic datasets.

papers.title: Minimax-Optimal Policy Regret in Partially Observable Markov Games
papers.contribution: Achieves Õ(√T) policy regret with explicit dependence on horizon, adversary memory, and aggregate Eluder dimension, matched by lower bound up to logarithmic factors.

papers.title: Near Optimal Robust Federated Learning Against Data Poisoning Attack
papers.contribution: The approach achieves O-tilde((1/n)^{1/2} + (d/mn)^{1/2}) attack loss in IID and O-tilde((1/gamma)^{1/2} + (1/n)^{1/2} + (d/mn)^{1/2}) in non-IID settings, matching lower bounds.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Regret for KL-Regularized Multi-Armed Bandits
papers.contribution: First high-probability regret bound with linear K dependence and complete characterization across all regularization intensity regimes.

papers.title: Nearly-Optimal Bandit Learning in Stackelberg Games with Side Information
papers.contribution: Achieves O(T^{1/2}) regret under bandit feedback, an improvement over previously known rates, with empirical outperformance on numerical simulations.

papers.title: Neural Logistic Bandits
papers.contribution: Regret bounds growing with effective dimension rather than ambient dimension: O-tilde(d-eff sqrt(kappa T)) and O-tilde(d-eff sqrt(T/kappa)), improving on existing results with minimal kappa dependence.

papers.title: Next-Token Prediction and Regret Minimization
papers.contribution: Shows modest context-window increase restores robustification, and small transformers can be trained to represent robustified distributions.

papers.title: Nonparametric Contextual Online Bilateral Trade
papers.contribution: Achieve regret Õ(T^((d-1)/d)) under one-bit feedback and strong budget balance with matching lower bounds demonstrating tightness.

papers.title: On the Emergence of Implicit Curriculum in RLVR Learning Dynamics
papers.contribution: Shows theoretically that RLVR training enters a 'relay' regime with smooth difficulty spectra where persistent gradient signals on easier problems make slightly harder ones tractable, validated via synthetic experiments.

papers.title: On the Learnability of Test-Time Adaptation: A Recovery Complexity Perspective
papers.contribution: Derives order-wise matching lower and upper bounds on recovery complexity, revealing fundamental limits of TTA and an intrinsic adaptivity-information trade-off with unified learnability guarantees.

papers.title: One-Shot Weighted Ensemble Estimation for Federated Quantile Regression: Optimal Statistical Guarantees under Heterogeneous Structured Data
papers.contribution: Achieves asymptotic normality with uniformly minimum variance and enjoys strong out-of-sample generalization compared to baselines across various quantile levels.

papers.title: Online Contract Design With Unknown Technology
papers.contribution: Enables practical online learning algorithms for contract design by avoiding exponential scaling in problem instance size.

papers.title: Online Decision Making with Generative Action Sets
papers.contribution: The algorithm achieves optimal regret of O(T^(d/(d+2))d^(d/(d+2)) + d√(T log T)), providing the first sublinear regret bound for online learning with expanding action spaces.

papers.title: Online Learning and Equilibrium Computation with Ranking Feedback
papers.contribution: Shows sublinear regret is impossible with instantaneous rankings; proposes algorithms for time-average rankings under additional assumptions on utility variation.

papers.title: Online Learning with Recency: Algorithms for Sliding-window Streaming Multi-armed Bandits
papers.contribution: Sharp memory-regret trade-offs for single-pass algorithms and efficient approximate best-arm finding under limited memory.

papers.title: Online Packet Scheduling with Deadlines and Learning
papers.contribution: Provides algorithms with α-regret upper bounds of O(√KT) matching lower bounds for standard bandits; for 2-bounded deadline instances achieves provably tightest competitive ratio and breaks the 1.618 barrier.

papers.title: Online Prediction of Stochastic Sequences with High Probability Regret Bounds
papers.contribution: Establishes vanishing high-probability regret bounds with similar form to prior expectation bounds and proves an impossibility result on improving the δ exponent.

papers.title: Optimal Decision-Making Based on Prediction Sets
papers.contribution: We first characterize the minimax optimal policy for a fixed prediction set, showing that it balances the worst-case loss inside the set with a penalty for potential losses outside the set

papers.title: Optimal Unconstrained Self-Distillation in Ridge Regression: Strict Improvements, Precise Asymptotics, and One-Shot Tuning
papers.contribution: Characterizes optimal mixing weight in terms of risk derivative, derives exact risk asymptotics in proportional limits for anisotropic covariance, and proposes consistent one-shot tuning without grid search.

papers.title: Personalized Collaborative Learning with Affinity-Based Variance Reduction
papers.contribution: Reduces sample complexity over independent learning by max{n^-1, δ} and automatically interpolates between federated linear speedup and independent learning baseline.

papers.title: Powerful and Theoretically Guaranteed Independence Testing on Heterogeneous Federated Clients
papers.contribution: Provides theoretically sound test with proven correctness; superior performance on synthetic and real-world datasets.

papers.title: Prediction-Powered Adaptive Inference with Pretrained AI Models for Contextual Bandits
papers.contribution: Enables valid confidence intervals and hypothesis tests with asymptotic variance no worse than labeled-only baseline and strictly smaller when predictions are informative.

papers.title: RLAP-CLIP: Continual Multimodal Learning with Prototype Adaptation and Difficulty-Aware Routing
papers.contribution: We propose RLAP-CLIP, which addresses these limitations through three components.

papers.title: Regret Minimization With a Crowd of Awakening Experts
papers.contribution: We provide optimal or near-optimal regret bounds with matching lower bounds for both stochastic and adversarial awakening expert problems.

papers.title: Revenue Guarantees of No-Swap-Regret Dynamics in First Price Auctions
papers.contribution: The work establishes the first polynomial convergence rates on revenue generated by no-swap regret bidders, with time-averaged revenue approaching v₂ - Θ(1/k) - Θ(ε).

papers.title: Revenue Maximization Under Sequential Price Competition Via The Estimation Of $s$-Concave Demand Functions
papers.contribution: Prices converge to Nash equilibrium at O(T^-1/7) rate with O(T^5/7) regret, establishing equilibrium existence under shape constraints.

papers.title: Self-Distillation Enables Continual Learning
papers.contribution: SDFT consistently outperforms SFT on skill learning and knowledge acquisition tasks, achieving higher new-task accuracy while substantially reducing catastrophic forgetting.

papers.title: The Cost of Information: Phase Transitions in Contextual Bandits with Paid Observations
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical characterization of when free observations improve regret rates and designs meta-controller achieving near-optimal performance across all budget regimes.

papers.title: The Cost of Learning Under Multiple Change Points
papers.contribution: Achieves nearly minimax-optimal regret guaranteed to closely match novel information-theoretic lower bound for multiple change point learning.

papers.title: The Gaussian-Head OFL Family: One-Shot Federated Learning from Client Global Statistics
papers.contribution: GH-OFL delivers state-of-the-art robustness and accuracy under strong non-IID skew while remaining data-free.

papers.title: The Sample Complexity of Online Reinforcement Learning: A Multi-model Perspective
papers.contribution: Algorithm achieves policy regret of O(N ε² + ln(m(ε))/ε²) in general settings and O(√Np) for parametrized systems, recovering results for linear systems.

papers.title: Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models
papers.contribution: Identifies key findings about dataset quality requirements at different training stages, validated on large nonlinear architectures.

papers.title: Tighter Regret Lower Bound for Gaussian Process Bandits with Squared Exponential Kernel in Hypersphere
papers.contribution: Shows any algorithm suffers Omega(sqrt(T(ln T)^d(ln ln T)^-d)) cumulative regret and improves information gain upper bounds to O((ln T)^(d+1)(ln ln T)^-d), achieving near-optimality.

papers.title: Towards a Sharp Analysis of Learning Offline $f$-Divergence-Regularized Contextual Bandits
papers.contribution: Achieves Õ(ε⁻¹) sample complexity under single-policy concentrability, surpassing prior Õ(ε⁻²) bounds and providing near-matching lower bounds.

papers.title: Transformers with RL or SFT Provably Learn Sparse Boolean Functions, But Differently
papers.contribution: Reveals that RL learns the entire CoT chain simultaneously while SFT learns step-by-step, providing mechanistic insights into RL vs. SFT differences.

papers.title: Turning Back Without Forgetting: Selective Backward Refinement for Parameter-Efficient Continual Learning
papers.contribution: SABER consistently achieves positive backward transfer while maintaining strong overall average performance across continual learning benchmarks on T5-Large, LLaMA, and Qwen.

papers.title: Understanding the Gaps in Satisficing Bandits
papers.contribution: Proves satisficing pseudo-regret of O(sum_{i:Delta_i>Delta_*} ln(K/Delta_*)/Delta_i) and establishes a near-matching lower bound.

papers.title: Universal Multiclass Transductive Online Learning
papers.contribution: Proves that learnable classes have either bounded or logarithmically increasing mistake rates, and extends results to agnostic and stochastic settings.

papers.title: Variance-Dependent Regret Lower Bounds for Contextual Bandits
papers.contribution: Overcomes limitations of prior work with improved lower bound of Ω(d√(Σσ²_k)/log K) that closes gap with existing upper bounds.

papers.title: What Preferences Can—and Cannot—Predict in Multi-Agent Online Learning
papers.contribution: The work proves dynamic stability equivalence for subgames and identifies conditions under which payoff-based leaklessness guarantees stability.

papers.title: When Is Diversity Rewarded in Cooperative Multi-Agent Learning?
papers.contribution: Proves that for broad reward families heterogeneity advantage collapses to a convexity test; HetGPS validates theory on different environments and connects theoretical insights to practical MARL reward design.
